title: Microphase hiring rebase and rate sensitivity playbook
body:
Purpose:
This is a tactical spreadsheet-style playbook to rebase hiring over a 12-week microphase, evaluate pricing 'kicker' options (small % changes tied to feature tiers), and show the impact on burn and runway. Intended as a live working artifact for FY26 Q3 contingency planning. High-level aim: preserve critical hiring for product and infra while creating a shallow price lever that recovers unit margin with minimal churn risk.

Key assumptions (quick):
- Starting runway (today): 14.8 months at baseline spend
- Baseline monthly net burn: $2.1M (payroll + infra + cloud + ops)
- Average fully-loaded senior eng hire (annual): $260k -> monthly ~ $21.7k
- Contractor FTE cost equivalent: 1.0 contractor = $13k/month
- Pricing kicker options tested: +3%, +6%, +10% applied to premium route only (~20% of revenue)
- Elasticity: assume 0.4 elasticity in first 90 days for premium route (conservative)
- One-time churn assumption for any price move: 1.5% of premium customers (front-loaded)

Scenario matrix (rows are scenarios; columns show quick calc outputs). All numbers rounded.

Columns: Scenario | New Hires (12w) | Contractors (12w) | Payroll Δ/mo | Contractor Δ/mo | Price Δ (%) | Expected Rev Δ/mo | Net Burn Δ/mo | New Runway (months) | Action priority

1) Baseline (no change) | 12 hires | 0 contractors | +$260k | $0 | 0% | $0 | +$260k | 13.1 | Low
2) Microphase pause (shift hiring 6->12w) | 6 hires | 6 contractors | +$130k | +$78k | 0% | $0 | +$208k | 13.6 | Medium
3) Partial pause + +3% kicker | 6 hires | 4 contractors | +$130k | +$52k | +3% premium | +$48k | +$134k | 14.2 | High
4) Aggressive pause + +6% kicker | 3 hires | 6 contractors | +$65k | +$78k | +6% premium | +$96k | +$47k | 15.9 | High
5) Soft hire + +10% kicker + targeted credits | 10 hires | 2 contractors | +$217k | +$26k | +10% premium | +$160k | +$83k | 14.6 | Medium
6) Headcount freeze + product discount swap | 0 hires | 8 contractors | $0 | +$104k | -2% across tier | -$32k | -$136k | 17.0 | Low

Interpretation notes (walkthrough):
- Baseline shows immediate runway contraction because new hires front-load payroll. Baseline runway 13.1 months (ex: worst-case cadence).
- Scenario 2 reduces payroll by substituting contractors, preserving throughput at higher cost but smoothing long-term org commitments. Net runway improves marginally.
- Scenario 3 is the preferred operational compromise: modest pause + small price kicker targeted at premium route recovers ~36% of extra monthly payroll. With 0.4 elasticity and 1.5% churn, revenue uptick is net positive across month 1–3 window.
- Scenario 4 is the 'defensive' posture that buys more runway with fewer hires and stronger price lift; risk: customer backlash and partner escalations. Prioritize only if Q3 usage surges >25% month-on-month.
- Scenario 5 is optimistic: uses a larger pricing move but pairs with targeted credits to high-value customers (offset churn). Admin complexity and CS load higher.
- Scenario 6 is a non-price approach that freezes hires and leans on contractors; saves cash but reduces medium-term product velocity.

Mini-model (formulas used):
- Payroll Δ/mo = hires_this_month * avg_monthly_full_loaded_cost
- Contractor Δ/mo = contractors_this_month * avg_monthly_contractor_cost
- Expected Rev Δ/mo = premium_revenue_base * share_premium * price_delta * (1 - churn_frontload) * (1 - elasticity * price_delta)
  (Note: simplifying continuous elasticity and immediate churn into a single-month effect for quick planning)
- Net Burn Δ/mo = Payroll Δ/mo + Contractor Δ/mo - Expected Rev Δ/mo
- New Runway (months) = current_cash / (baseline_burn + Net Burn Δ/mo)

Action checklist (week-by-week cadence for next 12 weeks):
- Week 0: Exec alignment on permissible price range, sign-off on customer comms framework (owners: Finance, Product, Legal).
- Week 1: Prepare billing system feature-flag for premium route price kicker; QA path for instant rollback. (owners: Platform eng + Billing)
- Week 2: CS + Sales readout + targeted customer segment list for credits. (owners: CS lead)
- Week 3: Implement contractor sourcing pipeline to cover paused hires (talent ops).
- Week 4: Dry run rollout to 3 pilot customers; monitor usage and churn signals. (owners: Growth + Analytics)
- Week 5–8: Rollout if KPIs within thresholds; otherwise, revert and move to defensive pause.
- Week 9–12: Re-evaluate hiring plan vs. usage; present updated 90-day runway to execs.

Risks & mitigation: 
- Billing rollback complexity -> Mitigation: feature-flag and customer-friendly wording, 2-day rollback SLA.
- Competitive PR -> Mitigation: small % change, limited to premium route, accompanied by value messaging (SLA/throughput benefits).
- CS workload spike -> Mitigation: pre-baked credit templates and dedicated CS rotation.

Open questions (to resolve by Week 1):
- Exact premium revenue baseline (need segment-level monthly ARR slice) -> ACTION: Analytics to surface by 2026-04-15.
- Legal review of region-specific price adjustments (EU consumer protections) -> ACTION: Legal by 2026-04-18.
- Thresholds for rollback (acceptable churn %) -> ACTION: Growth to propose thresholds.

Appendix (quick sensitivity append):
- If elasticity is lower (0.2), +6% yields ~+128k revenue/mo (vs 96k assumed) -> runway improvement +1.2 months relative to baseline scenario 4.
- If churn is 3% one-time, revenue recovery drops ~40% and net benefit may become negative for >6% moves.

Short-term ask to execs:
1) Approve go/no-go for Scenario 3 as default contingency.
2) Allocate up to $60k one-time CS buffer for credits and increased support during rollout.
3) Approve contractor headcount flex line for up to 10 FTE-equivalent across QA and infra.

Notes to self (working):
- Hook in the detailed segment ARR table from Analytics next version of this sheet.
- Consider mapping pricing kicker to retention features (e.g., reserved throughput) not raw % to reduce perceived price increase.
- Track telemetry: sign-ups, cancellations, support volume, NPS delta for 90 days.

Change log:
- 2026-04-12 Priya Rao created initial skeleton and scenario outputs.
- 2026-04-15 Ethan Walker added contractor cost estimates and alternative scenario 6.
- 2026-04-20 Marisol Vega inserted rollout checklist and legal action items.

This file is intentionally compact; translate to a tabular sheet in the financial workbook for automated per-day burn simulation.
